newsitem.title: CANADA: Hydro-Quebec says nine-months net C$200 mln.
newsitem.headline: Hydro-Quebec says nine-months net C$200 mln.

text.p: Quebec government-owned Hydro-Quebec said on Tuesday that its net income in the first nine months of the year was C$200 million, a 75 percent increase from the year earlier period.
Hydro-Quebec also said it expected to realize net income of C$516 million for the year, as requested by the Quebec government.

Hydro-Quebec said revenues from total electricity sales for the first nine months rose 1.4 percent to C$5.6 billion. While revenues from electricity sales in Quebec rose 2.9 percent, due to increased demand and colder weather in 1996, revenues from electricity sales outside Quebec fell 13 percent to C$440 million.
The utility said it considerably reduced the number of short-term transactions with neighboring systems in order to reconstitute the energy reserve depleted by low runoff in 1995.

Hydro-Quebec said operating expenses fell by C$106 million or 8.1 percent in the first nine months of 1995 to C$1.2 billion. Those savings offset the C$122 million increase in depreciation, amortization and decommissioning expenses from the commissioning of facilities at Phase II of the La Grande complex.

The fall in interest rates had a beneficial effect on floating-rate debt payments, although the commissionings of new facilities undertaken since 1995 continued to pressure interest expense, the utility said. Financial expenses during the period were C$2.4 billion, down C$54 million from the first nine months of 1995.
Hydro-Quebec is wholly owned by the Quebec government. It generates, distributes and markets most of the electricity in the Canadian province.
